title: Coherence normalization from endomorphism detection
statement: Let B be a preorder with a least element b0, P a Cat-valued pseudofunctor on its locally discrete bicategory, A a category, and J_b:P(b)→A functors. Suppose each arrow f:b→c has a supplied natural isomorphism J_b≅P(f)J_c, and precomposition by P(b0→b) is bijective on natural endomorphisms of J_b. Then one can choose comparisons e_f satisfying the unit and composition equations for the actual pseudofunctor constraints: e_id followed by J(mapId) is identity, and e_fg followed by J(mapComp) equals e_f followed by e_g on P(f).

source.place: Weil II (1.1.1) d), pp. 146-147, categorical coherence implicit in coefficient extension; agent proof using Mathlib pseudofunctor unit and associativity axioms

proof.text: Divide a desired isomorphism after precomposition by any supplied comparison. Lift the resulting endomorphism and its inverse using bijectivity, and use injectivity to show they are inverse. This also proves injectivity on isomorphisms with a fixed comparison target.

Choose comparisons b_c from the least fibre to each c. Define the required precomposition of e_f as b_c inverse, b_d, the composition constraint of P, and the functor associator; lift it by the preceding construction.

For identity arrows compare with the inverse of the mapped unit constraint. Whiskering reduces equality to the right unit law of P. For composition substitute the lifted comparisons, use naturality, cancel adjacent b maps, and apply the associativity coherence axiom of P. Thinness makes the composites from b0 the same arrow.

theorem Pseudofunctor.coherentFiberComparisons_of_endWhisker {B : Type*} [Preorder B]
    (b₀ : B) (hb : ∀ b : B, b₀ ≤ b)
    (P : Pseudofunctor (LocallyDiscrete B) Cat.{d + 1, d + 2})
    {A : Type*} [Category A] (J : ∀ b : B, P.obj ⟨b⟩ ⥤ A)
    (a : ∀ {b c : B} (f : b ⟶ c), J b ≅ (P.map f.toLoc).toFunctor ⋙ J c)
    (h : ∀ b : B, Function.Bijective (fun u : J b ⟶ J b ↦
      whiskerLeft (P.map (homOfLE (hb b)).toLoc).toFunctor u)) :
    ∃ e : ∀ {b c : B} (f : b ⟶ c), J b ≅ (P.map f.toLoc).toFunctor ⋙ J c,
      (∀ (b : B) (X : P.obj ⟨b⟩),
        (e (𝟙 b)).hom.app X ≫ (J b).map ((P.mapId ⟨b⟩).hom.toNatTrans.app X) = 𝟙 _) ∧
      (∀ {b c d : B} (f : b ⟶ c) (g : c ⟶ d) (X : P.obj ⟨b⟩),
        (e (f ≫ g)).hom.app X ≫
            (J d).map ((P.mapComp f.toLoc g.toLoc).hom.toNatTrans.app X) =
          (e f).hom.app X ≫ (e g).hom.app ((P.map f.toLoc).toFunctor.obj X))
